presentation_feature: Existing and planned data center locations
preferred_open_source: OpenStreetMap plus Wikidata plus operator announcements and permitting records
rationale: No single open national registry exists. Combining OSM and structured public references is the most reproducible public baseline.
known_limitations: Coverage is incomplete and weaker than Baxtel for planned and under-construction sites.

rationale: EIA-860 is the authoritative public U.S. generator inventory with operable and proposed tabs.
known_limitations: Retired coverage is lagged and some transformation is required to create a clean spatial layer.

rationale: These public EIA datasets expose proposed, retired, and canceled generator states that align with the presentation's planned and retired generator features.
known_limitations: Still requires preprocessing and coordinate normalization.

rationale: OSM is an open national base-map source with broad coverage for transport and built-structure features.
known_limitations: Coverage quality varies by region and building attributes are inconsistent.

preferred_open_source: OpenStreetMap power lines plus public utility or federal line inventories where available
rationale: OSM gives a reproducible national baseline and can be filtered by voltage where tags exist.
known_limitations: Voltage tags are incomplete and the result is weaker than a curated transmission model.

preferred_open_source: OpenStreetMap substations plus state utility GIS where available
rationale: Open public mapping can provide a reproducible national baseline for substation proximity.
known_limitations: Distribution-level coverage is inconsistent and exact capacity or voltage metadata is sparse.

preferred_open_source: FCC Broadband Data Collection plus OSM telecom layers
rationale: FCC provides national broadband availability while OSM can contribute route-like telecom features.
known_limitations: Availability does not equal fiber-route geometry
column8: so this is only a proxy for exact fiber proximity.

preferred_open_source: Public pipeline mapping portals plus OSM
rationale: Publicly accessible pipeline maps can support a coarse proximity layer.
known_limitations: Exact downloadable national centerline access may vary; route fidelity and attributes may be limited.

preferred_open_source: State public service commission service territory layers where available
rationale: State utility service territories are the best public analogue for retail gas service areas.
known_limitations: There is no clean national open standard layer; state-by-state assembly is required.

preferred_open_source: County assessor parcel values or public land-value proxies
rationale: Public parcel or assessor data is the closest open analogue to land value where coverage exists.
known_limitations: No harmonized national open dataset exists and jurisdictions vary widely.

rationale: QCEW and LEHD provide public employment and worker-density proxies for construction-related labor supply.
column8: not a direct data center construction workforce measure.

preferred_open_source: Regional wage and price proxies built from public labor data
rationale: Public labor and regional cost proxies can support a weaker affordability feature when direct commercial construction-cost datasets are unavailable.
known_limitations: No public national dataset reproduces data center dollars-per-MW construction cost directly.

preferred_open_source: FEMA National Risk Index or related FEMA risk products
rationale: FEMA risk products are the most direct public analogue for multi-hazard loss screening.
known_limitations: Exact match to the presentation's loss-rate feature still needs transformation design.

rationale: USGS public water datasets are the best open starting point for water-related screening.
known_limitations: Public water-use summaries are often coarser than the site-level water-availability concept used in the presentation.
